text:
Mark Scheifele is in his 15th season in Winnipeg and, according to Daily Faceoff, just tied the Jets' franchise points record. He celebrated the week the way the Jets have been celebrating everything lately: a buzzer-beating power-play winner against Tampa, a five-game point streak and a team that won five straight.

Our numbers think he's due more goals, not fewer. He has 6 on 8.3 expected, shooting 14% against a talent range near 16%, and his chances in the last ten games (5.1 expected goals) are well above his usual rate. Fourteen points in ten games is about three more than we'd expect at his ice time, but the assists are coming from real play, not on-ice luck.

He's still one of the league's best passers. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 99th percentile among forwards in primary shot assists last season. The old knock still applies too: Evolving-Hockey had opponents generating more against him than against almost any forward. Winnipeg owns 53% of five-on-five expected goals with him on. Watch the defensive side of that number, because it decides whether this line is good or great.
headline: Scheifele, still Winnipeg's engine at 33
